predecessors.text: the fortress of Kalanjara, 'captured Kalinjar from the Kalachuris' before 954

successors.name: Khalji dynasty
successors.text: Bundelkhand; the infobox names the Ghurid dynasty and the Mamluk dynasty (Delhi) as successors, the dynasty's titles in 1288-1315 'do not indicate a high political status'

ledger.x: c. 831: Nannuka founds the Chandela kingdom around Khajuraho. Infobox 'Founded: c. 831'; Nannuka 'the founder of the dynasty, was the ruler of a small kingdom centered around Khajuraho' (reign 831-845). A Pratihara vassal at first. Region cut from 80 to 50 km in the repair of 2026-10-19: the 80 km disc held Kalinjar…
836: the Chandelas rule as Pratihara vassals.

c. 950: Dhanga formally founds Chandela sovereignty. 'Dhanga (r. c. 950-999)... his records do not mention any Pratihara overlord. This indicates that Dhanga formally established the Chandela sovereignty.' Yashovarman 'continued to acknowledge the Pratihara suzerainty, but became practically independent'. The…

c. 950: the Chandelas take Gwalior. Gurjara-Pratihara page: 'the Chandelas captured the strategic fortress of Gwalior in central India around 950.' (The Chandela page does not credit Yashovarman or Dhanga with Gwalior; it has the Kachchhapaghatas of Gwalior as Chandela subordinates who 'probably gave up their…

c. 950 (bridge): the rest of Cliopatria's 960 shape (Bundelkhand and the Doab margin) beyond the home district and Kalinjar. Moved from 960 to 950 in the repair of 2026-10-19: Dhanga's accession (c. 950), the start of keyframe 950 and the end of the Pratihara vassalage. The page: Dhanga 'formally established the…

c. 1035 (bridge): Gwalior leaves the Chandela sphere. 'The Kachchhapaghatas of Gwalior probably gave up their allegiance to the Chandelas during this period'. Added 2026-10-19 to close the Gwalior gain of 950.

c. 1035: the Kalachuris conquer eastern parts. At the end of Vidyadhara's reign (1003-1035): 'the Ghaznavid invasions had weakened the Chandela kingdom' and the Kalachuri king Gangeya-deva 'conquered eastern parts of the kingdom'. Vidyadhara had paid tribute to Mahmud of Ghazni.…

c. 1070: Kirttivarman wins the east back. 'His younger brother Kirttivarman resurrected the Chandela power by defeating Lakshmi-Karna' (reign 1060-1100); Kirttivarman page (opened 2026-10-19): 'S. K. Mitra dates the battle to c. 1070 CE.' The first version used his accession, 1060 (confidence 1). The page names no…
1085 (bridge): 28 cells on the northern edge pass to the Gahadavalas, whose Cliopatria row begins in 1085.

c. 1182-83: Prithviraj Chauhan invades. 'the Chahamana ruler Prithviraj Chauhan invaded the Chandela kingdom' and 'sacked Mahoba'; the Madanpur inscriptions of 1182-83 corroborate the raid. No annexation (Talbot) or a short one.
1183: the raid ends; Paramardi remains king.

wars.name: Ghaznavid invasions of the Chandela kingdom
wars.outcome: Vidyadhara 'killed the king of Kannauj (possibly Rajyapala) for fleeing his capital instead of fighting the Ghaznavid invader'; 'Mahmud later invaded Vidyadhara's kingdom', which 'ended with Vidyadhara paying tribute to Mahmud' (Muslim sources).

wars.name: Chandela-Kalachuri wars
wars.outcome: Gangeya-deva took the eastern parts; Lakshmi-Karna subjugated Devavarman; Kirttivarman defeated Lakshmi-Karna (1060-1100); Madanavarman defeated Gaya-Karna and possibly annexed northern Baghelkhand, lost to Narasimha (undated).

wars.name: Chandela-Paramara wars
wars.outcome: Sallakshanavarman raided the Paramaras; Naravarman lost territory to the Chandelas (Paramara page); Madanavarman captured the Bhilsa territory, recaptured by Lakshmivarman (undated).

wars.name: Chaulukya-Chandela conflict
wars.outcome: Jayasimha 'reached as far as the Chandela kingdom'; the conflict 'appears to have been inconclusive, as records of both the kingdoms claim victory'.

wars.name: Prithviraj III-Chandela war (Mahoba)
wars.outcome: Prithviraj invaded and sacked Mahoba in 1182-83 without a lasting annexation.

wars.name: Ghurid conquest of Kalinjar
wars.outcome: Aibak besieged Kalinjar in 1202 or 1203; the garrison surrendered on 27 April 1203; Trailokyavarman had the fort again by 1205.

wars.name: Ghurid expedition against Kalinjar
wars.outcome: A commander's expedition of 1233/34 plundered the town below the fort; 'Taisi does not appear to have actually captured the fortress'.

certainty.note: No treaty line appears on any page opened.
